clue.text: Provide food having inserted the medical tube

indicators.note: the word for providing food takes another word put inside it

blocks.note: to cater is to supply food
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hospital patient is fed through a tube put in for the purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' is both part of the definition's phrasing and the inserted word: CA(THE)TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A catheter is a thin flexible tube passed into the body to drain or deliver fluids.

clue.text: Private school includes curriculum subject

indicators.note: one word holds another within it, so the school word wraps the subject

blocks.note: a school of thought is a sect
RE is Religious Education, a subject on British school timetables

explanation.surface: An independent school's timetable includes some particular subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private school' reads as one phrase, but 'Private' is the definition and 'school' means a sect: SEC(RE)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something private is kept hidden from others, the adjective sense of secret.

clue.text: May need irons released to participate in exercise, right?

definitions.text: May need irons released to participate in exercise, right?

indicators.note: freed letters are let loose and fall into a new order
joining in means going inside the exercise word

blocks.note: PE is physical education
these letters rearranged
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone shackled asks whether they may have the leg irons off to join in the exercise period.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a shackled inmate wanting to join the exercise yard, while the wordplay puts rearranged IRONS inside PE and adds R.
explanation.definitionFit: A convict in fetters would need them taken off before joining in exercise, so the whole clue paints a jailed person.

clue.text: Tomorrow fruit topping will be changed

indicators.note: the top letter of the word is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: a common fruit

explanation.surface: A note that the fruit decoration on a dessert will be swapped tomorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: Change the first letter of BANANA to M. The clue does not supply the M; crossing letters and the definition settle it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mañana is Spanish for tomorrow, borrowed into English, often implying some vague later time.

clue.text: Wine gives a sign of something lacking when litre is bottled

indicators.note: being bottled means being enclosed, so the litre goes inside the sign

blocks.note: a caret is the proofreader's mark showing where something is missing
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: Bottling wine by the litre seems to leave a shortfall.
explanation.walkthrough: A caret (^) marks the spot where text has been left out; put L inside to get C(L)ARET.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: Repeated first half of American country dance

indicators.note: only the opening half of the word is kept, the rest dropped
the kept chunk is written twice in a row

blocks.note: a country in North America

explanation.surface: A country dance from America, done over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country dance' looks like one phrase, but 'country' belongs to the wordplay: half of CANADA, twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The cancan is a high-kicking dance made famous in Parisian music halls.

clue.text: Branch of army occupying city for a brief time

indicators.note: an army occupying a place sits inside it

blocks.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England
RE is the Royal Engineers, a branch of the British Army

explanation.surface: A unit of the army holds a city for a short spell.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is a historic spa city in the west of England; 'for' just links the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A breath, as in a pause for breath, is a very short moment of time.

clue.text: Impression made by house overlooking lake - unfavourable!

indicators.note: in a down entry, being above something means coming before it

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
L is the abbreviation for lake
a low opinion is an unfavourable one

explanation.surface: An estate agent complains that a lakeside house creates a bad impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impression' sounds like an opinion, but here it is a dent in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A hollow is a depression or dip, the kind of mark pressed into a soft surface.

clue.text: US philanthropist is tower of strength taking English bloke in tow

indicators.note: having something in tow means it follows on behind

blocks.note: a dependable person is a rock
E is the abbreviation for English
informal spelling of fellow

explanation.surface: A wealthy benefactor is a pillar of support, with an Englishman tagging along.
explanation.definitionFit: John D. Rockefeller was an American oil tycoon famed for giving away vast sums to charitable causes.

clue.text: 'ave a yearning, we hear, for something secure

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

blocks.note: hanker, with the h dropped as the apostrophe in 'ave signals

explanation.surface: A dropped-aitch speaker longs for stability.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'ave tells you to drop the H, so 'hanker' becomes 'anker', which says the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor holds a ship firmly in place, and figuratively is anything that gives stability.

clue.text: Snag with ends of two cables knotted

indicators.note: the two end letters of the word are kept
knotted things are twisted out of order

blocks.note: the first and last letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: A problem arises when the ends of two cables get tangled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends of two cables' reads as the cable ends, but the ends belong to the word 'two'.
explanation.definitionFit: A snag is an unexpected difficulty or hindrance that stands in the way.

clue.text: Philosopher's humbug listened to

indicators.note: something listened to is heard, not read

blocks.note: cant is hypocritical, sanctimonious talk

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a thinker's ideas as nonsense they have been made to hear.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanuel Kant was the eighteenth-century German thinker behind the Critique of Pure Reason.

clue.text: Accepting applause, as a toxophilite?

blocks.note: first meaning: bending forward to acknowledge clapping
second meaning: what an archer does, picking up the weapon

explanation.walkthrough: A toxophilite is an archer; the question mark flags the playful literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Performers bend at the waist to acknowledge an audience, while an archer literally picks up the weapon that shoots arrows.

clue.text: Anti-abortion judge to flourish

blocks.note: pro-life is the label of the anti-abortion movement
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: An anti-abortion judge is set to thrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To proliferate is to multiply rapidly and thrive, spreading in great numbers.

clue.text: Line that's golden, befitting top poet

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
aureate is a literary word for gold-coloured

explanation.surface: A golden line of verse is worthy of the nation's leading poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poet Laureate is the official national poet in Britain; as an adjective laureate means crowned with laurel, worthy of honour.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word describes someone crowned with laurels, worthy of distinction as the foremost poet.

clue.text: Heavy metal cask gents manoeuvred

indicators.note: things manoeuvred are moved about into new positions

blocks.note: a tun is a large barrel
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Men struggle to shift a heavy barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' suggests rock music, but it means a dense chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is a very dense metallic element, used in light filaments and hard alloys.

clue.text: Second attractive girl in the current fashion

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, an informal second
dish is slang for an attractive person

explanation.surface: A second pretty girl is dressed in the latest style.
explanation.definitionFit: Modish describes something stylish and up to date, conforming to what is popular now.

clue.text: Spittle allowed to get into cup

blocks.note: gob is British slang for a lump of spit
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: Someone permits saliva to land in a drinking vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get into' suggests putting one piece inside another, but the pieces are simply placed side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a drinking vessel with a stem and a foot, a type of cup.

clue.text: Wine reduction process is grating

blocks.note: port is a fortified Portuguese wine
a cull is a selective killing to reduce numbers
taken as written

explanation.surface: A wine-making step that reduces the liquid sounds harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grating' looks like an adjective meaning irritating, but it is the noun for a lattice of bars.
explanation.definitionFit: A portcullis is the heavy iron lattice dropped to seal a castle gateway.

clue.text: Interception upends two quadrupeds

indicators.note: turning something upside down in a down entry reads it from the bottom up

blocks.note: an elk and a cat, two four-legged animals

explanation.surface: A sporting intercept sends two four-legged animals flying.
explanation.definitionFit: In football or rugby, a tackle is a move to take the ball from an opponent, an interception of play.

clue.text: Temporarily relocate help

blocks.note: first meaning: to transfer a worker to another post for a time
to assist or back someone, as a supporter does

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is stressed on the second syllable (se-COND); the second is the usual pronunciation.
explanation.definitionFit: Staff can be moved to another department for a spell, and a backer supports a duellist or a motion.

clue.text: Recess will accommodate limited number all right

blocks.note: NO is the shortened form of number
OK means all right

explanation.surface: An alcove will hold a small number of people, which is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' signals the abbreviation of 'number'; 'will accommodate' just links the alcove to its pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small sheltered corner or alcove in a room.

clue.text: Unattached little girl's holiday island

blocks.note: Di is short for Diana, so a little girl's name with the possessive
Crete is a Greek island popular with tourists

explanation.surface: A young woman's vacation spot in the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: Don't confuse with discreet: discrete means separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Discrete means separate and distinct, not joined to other parts.

clue.text: Man initially occupying a corner in magnificent house

blocks.note: first meaning: a chess piece that starts the game in a corner square
second meaning: a grand fortified residence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece, and 'initially' means at the start of the game: the rook begins in a corner. 'Man initially' looks like an M.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook is also called by this name in chess, and the same word names a lord's fortified stately home.

clue.text: Title for important official with many slaves

blocks.note: HE is His Excellency, a form of address for ambassadors and governors
lots means a great many

explanation.surface: A grandee with an honorific owns a large number of servants.
explanation.definitionFit: Helots were the serf class of ancient Sparta, and the word now means any enslaved or downtrodden people.

clue.text: Eager camper may settle here

blocks.note: first meaning: keen and resolved
second meaning, split into two words: where someone camping beds down

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into IN TENT, where a camper settles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intent on a goal is keenly focused on it, while canvas shelter is literally where campers rest.
